items.mnemonic_text: A roof gathering people below it: a meeting, to meet.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>cocoon</radical> sealed in the locker room splits open, and a <radical>person</radical> steps out mid-stride, heading for the corner table. There, <radical>two</radical> chopsticks sit crossed and waiting, set for one more guest — the cocoon opened right on time, because someone was coming to meet them.
items.reading_mnemonic: At that corner table, a boy named <reading>Kai</reading> waves both arms so hard the chopsticks clatter, shouting <reading>かい</reading> down the hallway so his cocoon-fresh friend won't miss the table.
items.description: 会 and 今 share the same person-shaped lid on top, but diverge below it: 会 stacks two flat strokes above a closed loop that seals shut at the bottom, giving it a boxed look. 今 has one flat stroke and a hook that swoops open to the lower right — no closed loop anywhere in it.

items.mnemonic_text: A box repeating the same shape inside: the same.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A wide box drops onto the level <radical>ground</radical> right outside Koichi's konbini, three walls up and no floor, blocking the door. You crouch down to peer through its open front — that's exactly the <radical>wide box</radical> you know — and staring back out of the gloom is a <radical>mouth</radical>, yawning out the very order you were about to say yourself, word for word. Same ground, same box, same mouth: same.
items.reading_mnemonic: Back at Koichi's konbini, the mouth belongs to the onigiri baker, elbow-deep in <reading>dough</reading> behind the counter. Every time you ask what's going on, he just grunts <reading>どう</reading> without looking up — same shrug, same word, same batch of dough, every single time you ask.

items.mnemonic_text: A hand holding a skewer of tasks: a matter to handle.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>broom</radical> keeps shoving the indignant cat down the hallway, crumbs and cat alike skidding across the level <radical>ground</radical>, until the whole heap finally piles up in front of a <radical>mouth</radical> — which snaps wide open, mid-yawn, and reports the entire incident as one official matter, filed and done.
items.reading_mnemonic: In Sei's school hallway, a kid who watched the whole cat-and-broom pileup yelps <reading>jeez</reading>, then gets marched off to file it with the teacher as an official <reading>じ</reading> — a matter now on the record, whether he wanted it there or not.

items.mnemonic_text: A nose pointing at oneself: 'me', self.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The staring <radical>eye</radical> that watches everything finally gets curious about itself. It swivels all the way around until it's pressed right up against a cracked mirror in Sei's school bathroom, pupil to pupil with its own reflection — recognizing, for the very first time, itself.
items.reading_mnemonic: Still at that mirror, a boy named <reading>Jeeves</reading> catches his own stare looking back and mutters <reading>じ</reading> — jeez — mortified that of everyone in the school, he's the one caught staring at himself.
items.description: 自 opens with a short diagonal tick above the top-left corner of the box — a stroke that 目 simply doesn't have; 目 is a plain, evenly-ruled rectangle with two level bars inside. 白 carries that same top tick, but its box is shorter and squarer with only a single centered bar, reading flatter and more compact than 自's taller, narrower frame.

items.mnemonic_text: An altar (示) marking earth (土): a shrine, and by extension a company.
items.meaning_mnemonic: On orientation day, the new hires drive the <radical>earth</radical> signpost into the ground behind Grandma Kane's shrine, right beside the stone <radical>altar</radical> where offerings sit out for everyone to see. Stake in the soil, altar in front of it — that's a company: a group planted on its own ground, showing itself off to the world.
items.reading_mnemonic: Still behind the shrine, a new hire named <reading>Shae</reading> trips over the freshly staked signpost and yelps <reading>しゃ</reading> as she stumbles face-first into the altar's offering tray — her first day at the company already the stuff of legend.
items.description: 社 originally named the local earth god's shrine — the altar raised on a patch of claimed ground for a village's protector spirit. The word later stretched to cover any group organized around a shared institution, which is why it equally means a shrine and a company: the modern sense kept the idea of a formal body bound to a place, not the religious content.

items.mnemonic_text: Legs launching outward from a bow: departure, emitting.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Off the blocks, the <radical>outspread legs</radical> explode sideways and collapse into a wincing split. The racer's <radical>human legs</radical> land planted wide just as <radical>two</radical> chopsticks clatter off a dropped bento — chasing a train already hissing steam, pulling away without them.
items.reading_mnemonic: On the platform, a conductor named <reading>Hatsu</reading> slams the doors and yells <reading>はつ</reading> into his whistle as steam bursts from the wheels — one word, and the train is already gone.

items.mnemonic_text: An old man bent over a stick: a person.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Every day, the same stooped shuffle you know as <radical>old</radical> reappears at the crosswalk just as the sun climbs behind that little barred window marking a new <radical>day</radical>, and traffic idles while it crosses. Rain or shine, that shuffle is the one figure the neighborhood recognizes — not by name, just as a person who shows up every day.
items.reading_mnemonic: The driver stuck idling at that crosswalk, a man named <reading>Shuji</reading>, finally leans on his horn and shouts <reading>しゃ</reading> — shoo! — at the shuffling old figure, who doesn't even glance up before finishing the crossing at exactly the same pace.
items.description: 者 almost never stands alone as a word; it works as a suffix stitched onto a verb or field to name whoever does it, much the way English -er turns 'teach' into 'teacher'. Learning it as a floating idea of a person is the right starting point, but expect to meet it glued onto the end of something else far more often than by itself.

items.mnemonic_text: Earth (土) twisting like a snake (also): the ground.
items.meaning_mnemonic: On the mountain trail, the wooden signpost planted in the <radical>earth</radical> isn't alone — beside its base, the last coiled loop of a snake's tail sits frozen in that same dirt, simply continuing <radical>to be</radical>. Sign and tail, both staked into the same patch of soil: together they mark out this exact stretch as ground.
items.reading_mnemonic: Still on that trail, a hiker named <reading>Cheech</reading> stubs his toe on the signpost and yelps <reading>ち</reading> — cheese! — hopping backward straight into the motionless snake tail, which doesn't so much as flinch.

items.mnemonic_text: A workbench stacked with tools: one's trade, business.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>sheep</radical> plants its four stiff legs on the level <radical>ground</radical> beneath a <radical>tree</radical>, hangs a little sign off a low branch, and spends the whole day there chewing calmly through paperwork, unbothered and punctual, running its own steady little trade. This is the sheep's business.
items.reading_mnemonic: Every morning a regular customer named <reading>Geo</reading> strolls up to the sheep's stand under the tree, and the sheep bleats <reading>ぎょう</reading> back at him like a receipt stamping shut — same tree, same ground, same bleat, business as usual.

items.mnemonic_text: A flag on a pole pointing a direction.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture 方 as one warped signpost bolted into a crossroads. Its crossbar arm won't hold still — it spins in the wind until it locks facing one direction, and a lost traveler grabs the swinging arm just to have something to follow. One pole, one direction, and the person now walking it.
items.reading_mnemonic: An owl called <reading>Hoot</reading> lands on the swinging signpost's crossbar and states the obvious in one flat call, <reading>ほう</reading>, every single time the arm swings past true north.
items.description: 万 is simpler than it looks: one long horizontal capped by a single sweeping curve that swings down and left into a hook, nothing above it. 方 carries an extra short tick above its crossbar before the vertical stroke kicks left and hooks at the bottom — that top tick is the tell. No tick, it's 万; tick present, it's 方.

items.mnemonic_text: Earth (土) where the sun (陽 implied) opens up a place.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At the riverbank, someone hammers a signpost into the <radical>earth</radical>, staking out one square patch of level <radical>ground</radical>, and every <radical>day</radical> the sun climbs up right over that same stake, marking the exact spot all over again. Sun after sun, the marker never moves — that patch has become a place.
items.reading_mnemonic: A fisherman named <reading>Joe</reading> claims that same staked patch every single morning, plants his stool right on the marker, and grunts <reading>じょう</reading> at anyone who dares set foot on his place at the riverbank.

items.mnemonic_text: An axe (斤) beside a door (戸): the place where work is done.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Right outside the door that never latches, the raccoon-dented one still swinging on its hinge, stands a stump with the woodsman's <radical>axe</radical> still buried in it — nobody ever pulled it back out. Meet me by the axe that never came out, right by the <radical>door</radical> that won't shut: that spot is the place everyone in town can point to.
items.reading_mnemonic: A mailman circles the stump twice before he's sure, then stamps the address form with one flat syllable, <reading>しょ</reading>, like he's about to <reading>show</reading> you exactly where to stand, axe and swinging door included.

items.mnemonic_text: A stylized heart shape with three drips of feeling.
items.meaning_mnemonic: That dragging fishhook flicks upward one final time, flinging its three blood drops clear across the tackle box, and beneath the hook you can still feel it, thudding out of rhythm every time the line goes taut. The whole hook has become nothing but one wounded, thumping <radical>heart</radical>, still working even torn open.
items.reading_mnemonic: A dockside medic named <reading>Shin</reading> presses a stethoscope to the hook and hears it clearly, <reading>しん</reading>, <reading>しん</reading>, ragged but steady, the same wounded rhythm from the tackle box.
items.description: 必, the kanji for necessary, is this same wounded heart with one extra diagonal stroke slashed clean through it from upper right to lower left, like a blade cutting across where 心 has nothing but hook and blood. A line piercing straight through the middle marks 必; the bare hook and three loose drops with nothing crossing them is 心.

items.mnemonic_text: A roof (广) over a stopping point (占): a shop.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Nailed into the cliff with nothing underneath, that lean-to <radical>shelter</radical> gets a tenant: a tortoise who reads cracks in its own shell for <radical>divination</radical>, shouting today's fortune to anyone passing. A wide <radical>mouth</radical> yawns open below as the doorway, swallowing customers whole to hear it. Shelter, fortune-teller, doorway — it's officially a shop.
items.reading_mnemonic: A customer ducks through the yawning mouth-shaped doorway, drops exactly <reading>ten</reading> coins on the tortoise's card table, and gets his fortune shouted back in one flat syllable, <reading>てん</reading>, then returns every week for the same price.

items.mnemonic_text: A roof over a pig (豕): the traditional house.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The pigeon sliding belly-first down that slick <radical>roof</radical> shoots off the eaves and through an open window, landing on the <radical>pig</radical> mid belly-rub, legs already kicking the air in outrage. Pig and pigeon end up tangled on one floor under one roof — and a roof with a pig living underneath, indignities and all, is what makes a house a house.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kaa the fire-breathing crow perches on the power line outside that house, unimpressed by the racket inside. Every time the pig squeals and kicks at the ceiling, she tips her head back and lets out one flat <reading>か</reading> — a dry little <reading>kah</reading> of judgment, then goes back to smoking her own beak.

items.mnemonic_text: A roof (宀) reaching (至) to enclose a room.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A dart drifts across the room, finally tips into its slow dive, and thuds point-first into the floorboards, quivering upright exactly where it has come to <radical>arrive</radical>. It lands directly under the sagging edge of a slick <radical>roof</radical>, and the patch of floor boxed in by that overhang — dart standing sentry in the middle of it — becomes a room all its own.
items.reading_mnemonic: A landlady everyone calls <reading>Shitsu</reading> stomps in to inspect the new room, presses her ear to the dart still quivering in the floorboards, and grunts a flat <reading>しつ</reading> of approval before stamping the doorframe and moving to the next one.

items.mnemonic_text: A box enclosing plotted lines: a diagram, a map.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Trapped inside a solid <radical>enclosure</radical> — four unbroken walls, no door, no window, no way out no matter which way you circle — someone stops walking and starts scratching lines into the plaster instead, every corner already paced, every dead turn, inked onto the inside of the wall. That scribbled record of the walk is now a diagram, a map of nothing but itself.
items.reading_mnemonic: A surveyor everyone calls <reading>Zuzu</reading> gets called in to examine the scratched walls, traces one finger along the lines, and grunts a single <reading>ず</reading> of approval — first map she's ever seen that doubles as a cry for help.

items.mnemonic_text: Words (言) given a式 (form/ceremony): a formal test.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At the ceremony marking a new <radical>construction</radical> site, someone hammers the flagged <radical>stake</radical> into the dirt to mark exactly where the girder will go, then clears their throat and gives it a go — a shaky <radical>speech</radical>, words bubbling out of the mouth one line at a time, nobody rehearsed, just to see if it works. Stake planted, girder not even up yet, speech barely holding together: that shaky first attempt is the very definition of a try.
items.reading_mnemonic: A foreman named <reading>Shii</reading> paces around the ceremony, hissing a stressed <reading>し</reading> through his teeth every time the speech wobbles, certain the whole shaky test is about to collapse before the stake even settles into the ground.

items.mnemonic_text: A horse (馬) inspected all over (侴): to test, examine.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>horse</radical> gallops in, all boxy body and dust-kicking hooves, expecting a race. Instead a vet in a lab coat pins it to a scale, shines a light in its eyes, and checks its teeth one by one. The horse stamps and snorts, furious, but every inch of it gets examined before it's ever let out to run.
items.reading_mnemonic: Ken, the sword-collecting dog, guards the clinic door with a wall of antique blades gleaming behind him. Every time the horse tries to bolt past without finishing its checkup, Ken barks one sharp <reading>けん</reading> — <reading>Ken</reading> means nobody skips the exam.

items.mnemonic_text: An old man's staff (攵) guiding a child (孝): to teach.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>old</radical> teacher shuffles to the desk, unhurried, cane dragging. A <radical>child</radical> bursts in, arms flung wide, bundled and eager. The elder rears that cane back over one shoulder and cracks it down in one furious <radical>tap</radical> — the child freezes, listening. That crack is how you teach.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kyo, the new teaching assistant, flinches every time the cane cracks against the desk and yelps <reading>きょう</reading> before she can stop herself. By the third lesson the whole class waits for her <reading>Kyo</reading>-shaped shriek before they even hear the tap.

items.mnemonic_text: A field (田) sitting over the heart (心): thoughts forming.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You stand at the edge of your flooded <radical>rice field</radical>, its paths crossing the plots into a grid below you. Above it your wounded <radical>heart</radical> drags itself up and hovers there, thumping, while you stare at the grid, turning the harvest over one square at a time. That thumping stillness is what it looks like to think.
items.reading_mnemonic: A heron named Shi stands dead still over the rice field, chewing over something enormous. Every few minutes it snaps its beak and lets out one flat <reading>し</reading> — proof that all that stillness is <reading>Shi</reading>'s thought, not sleep.

items.mnemonic_text: A bow (弓) with its string pulled taut: to pull.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At the top of the mountain trail, past the improbable vending machine, an archer plants their feet and hauls back on a springy <radical>bow</radical>, bending its stacked-curve wood taut until the string bites into their fingers. That single act of hauling back is the whole meaning: to pull.
items.reading_mnemonic: A parrot named Inko perches on the vending machine and screeches <reading>いん</reading> the instant the string snaps taut, like an <reading>inn</reading> bell ringing for a guest who arrived too fast. Every hiker on the trail flinches at the sound before they even see the arrow.

items.mnemonic_text: Repeated breaths (可可) beside a yawning mouth (欠): a song.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You drag up Grandma Kane's mossy shrine steps, one <radical>ground</radical>-level stair at a time, powered by nothing but a <radical>lack</radical> of energy — the kind that ends in a yawn. At the top your <radical>mouth</radical> cracks wide open, and instead of a yawn, a full song pours out, echoing off the bell until every cat bolts.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kaa the fire-breathing crow lands on that same shrine bell mid-echo and answers your song with his own — not a caw but a scorched-throat <reading>か</reading>, <reading>Kaa</reading>, puffing a little ring of fire that singes the moss every time he hits the note.

items.mnemonic_text: A hand (扌) keeping something steady like a temple (寺): to hold.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>hand</radical> reaches in from the kanji's left edge and closes around the carpenter's ruler notched for a single <radical>inch</radical>, then rams its end down into the <radical>earth</radical> like the mossy shrine signpost, refusing to let go until the plot is measured. That white-knuckle grip is what it means: to hold.
items.reading_mnemonic: The groundskeeper who plants that ruler in the dirt every morning is named <reading>Jee</reading> — one flat syllable, <reading>じ</reading> — and he grunts it out loud each time he drives the measure into the ground, like a stamp confirming the hold is solid.

items.mnemonic_text: A person (亻) directing an official (吏): to use, to employ.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At the riverbank, a <radical>person</radical> plants both feet on one patch of <radical>ground</radical> and flings their <radical>mouth</radical> wide, bellowing orders at everyone scrubbing laundry in the shallows — never lifting a hand, just pointing. That bossy, hands-off stance is use: someone else's effort put to work on your command.
items.reading_mnemonic: Shiba the heron struts along that same riverbank, screeching orders of his own at the laundry crew like a tiny drill sergeant — the sound comes out as a piercing <reading>し</reading>, pure <reading>sheesh</reading>, every single time someone slacks off scrubbing.

items.mnemonic_text: A person (亻) in motion (動): working.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>person</radical> hauls up the mountain trail before dawn, one <radical>power</radical>-flexed arm dragging them past the vending machine, while the <radical>sun</radical> crawls across the sky, until both boots hit solid <radical>ground</radical> at the summit — soaked, aching, still not done. That sunrise-to-sunset climb is work.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the very top, a badger named <reading>Dobu</reading> slumps against that same vending machine and groans <reading>どう</reading> into the empty air — not a question, just the sound of a body that has decided the climb was too much work.

items.mnemonic_text: A person (亻) relying on old (昔) favors: to borrow.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Every <radical>day</radical>, as the sun climbs behind that little windowpane, a <radical>person</radical> strides in from the left and swipes <radical>two</radical> chopsticks off next door's table — promising to bring them back before the window goes dark again. It isn't stealing if you plan to return it; it's borrowing.
items.reading_mnemonic: The neighbor doesn't even look up. She just hears a stray cat named <reading>Shaku</reading> hiss <reading>しゃく</reading> from the doorway — her signal that her chopsticks have gone wandering again and will be back by dinner.
items.description: 借りる marks the side receiving something on loan — you end up holding an item that isn't yours yet. The opposite motion, handing something over to someone else, is a completely different kanji; don't let the shared idea of a loan blur which direction this one points.

items.mnemonic_text: Money (貝) replacing (代) what's missing: to lend.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>person</radical> strides in from the left, hammers a <radical>stake</radical> into the square, banner flapping, then tips open the clam-shell wallet — coins spilling from the <radical>money</radical> shell into open hands. The flag stays planted as a record of what was handed over, and to whom: this is lending.
items.reading_mnemonic: By the planted stake, a goat named <reading>Tai</reading> headbutts the empty shell and bleats <reading>たい</reading>, annoyed that all the coins are already gone — lent out before she got her share.
items.description: 貸す marks the side handing something over — you're the one giving up temporary use of something. The receiving side of that same transaction is a completely different kanji; keep the direction straight instead of leaning on the shared idea of a loan.

items.mnemonic_text: An arrow (矢) hitting the mouth's (口) point: to know for certain.
items.meaning_mnemonic: On Sei's sports field, an <radical>arrow</radical> streaks straight across the grass and thunks dead center into the target, and in that same instant your <radical>mouth</radical> snaps open with the answer — no hesitation, just the fact flying out as fast and true as the shot. That instant, certain hit is knowing something.
items.reading_mnemonic: Chibi the parrot roosts on that same target and shrieks <reading>ち</reading> the second the arrow lands, confirming the answer before you can even say it out loud — a sharp <reading>chee</reading> of certainty every time.

items.mnemonic_text: A woman (女) with her own (台) fresh start: to begin.
items.meaning_mnemonic: In the school locker room a silkworm has just sealed itself into its <radical>cocoon</radical>, when the star dancer bursts in yawning her <radical>mouth</radical> wide open, and mid-yawn her legs snap into that crossed, arms-flung stance of a <radical>woman</radical> about to perform. The cocoon splits open in that instant — this is where everything begins.
items.reading_mnemonic: The coach doesn't shout 'go' — she just says <reading>し</reading>, flat and clipped like the English word <reading>she</reading>, and that single syllable is the starting gun for the dancer, the silkworm, and everyone else still stretching by the lockers.

items.mnemonic_text: Thread (糸) wound to its winter (冬) finish: to end.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Grandma Kane sits on the shrine steps unspooling a length of <radical>thread</radical>, fibers fraying at the tip, and tied to the very end is a duckling towed along by its <radical>trailing foot</radical>, webbed foot skidding on the mossy stone. The spool runs out, the duckling skids to a stop at her feet, and there is nowhere left to go — that's the end.
items.reading_mnemonic: The instant the thread runs out, one of the shrine cats pounces and clamps its teeth on what's left of the duckling's lace like it's stealing a <reading>shoe</reading> — its triumphant yowl comes out as <reading>しゅう</reading>, the exact sound of the last stretch of thread giving way.

items.mnemonic_text: Grasping (⺈) at the heart (心): an urgent hurry.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>broom</radical>'s cat sleeps through it, so crumbs and cat skid down the hallway too fast to stop. Someone chasing it yanks the <radical>wrap</radical> tighter around the watermelon, and the jolt sets the <radical>heart</radical> — hook flicking, three drops flung loose — pounding in a full panicked sprint. Everyone hurries.
items.reading_mnemonic: Skidding into that same hallway, a courier pigeon named <reading>Cue</reading> can't stop in time and slams into the pile, wheezing out a strangled <reading>きゅう</reading> as crumbs and feathers go flying. He's always this late, and it's always this loud.

items.mnemonic_text: A person (土-like legs) bounding forward: to run.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The signpost that's usually planted still in the <radical>earth</radical>, crossbar and flat soil baseline undisturbed for years, suddenly rips itself loose and bolts down the mountain trail, dragging a ragged tail of dirt behind it, going faster than a plain wooden post has any business going. Somehow, it is now running.
items.reading_mnemonic: Hikers at the top of the trail gasp <reading>そう</reading> — a drawn-out sound just like the English word <reading>sew</reading> — as the loose signpost sprints past the vending machine, and one startled hiker keeps repeating it long after the post is gone.

items.mnemonic_text: Wings spread mid-motion: to fly.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture the whole character at once: two wings snapped open mid-beat, feathers combing the air on both sides, and a tail feather trailing straight back like it's still catching up. Nothing about the shape sits still — every stroke leans into the same direction, caught at the exact instant the ground lets go. That's fly.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the top of the mountain trail, past the lone vending machine, a paper crane named <reading>Hee</reading> catches an updraft and lifts clean off the ground. She lets out one thin <reading>ひ</reading> of surprise and doesn't come back down before the trail bends out of sight.

items.mnemonic_text: Water (氵) poured over first (先) rinse: to wash.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Someone plants their <radical>human legs</radical> wide in the shallows, bracing against the current. Three <radical>water</radical> droplets flick off a passing paintbrush into their face, then the whole current joins in, sluicing down their legs until every stain gets scrubbed clean. Wash.
items.reading_mnemonic: Downstream at the same riverbank, a heron named <reading>Sen</reading> watches the whole scrubbing with total calm, muttering one flat <reading>せん</reading> every time a sock goes under. She's heard it all before, standing on one leg exactly where the current runs coldest.

items.mnemonic_text: Bad luck (歹) beside a person collapsed: to die.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The raccoon is still airborne, gripping the bent <radical>spoon</radical> from that badly leveraged scoop of ice cream, and comes down hard on the already-cracked corner of <radical>death / bad luck</radical>. The bone gives way completely under the impact, nothing left to set or straighten. That's the whole story: die.
items.reading_mnemonic: Behind the register at Koichi's konbini, the cashier named <reading>She</reading> hears the crash and doesn't even look up, just breathes one flat <reading>し</reading> and rings up the shattered tub anyway. Nothing about tonight is going to surprise her.

items.mnemonic_text: A wandering road (辶) with a flag (斿) of fun: to play.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The bundled-up <radical>child</radical> flings both arms wide the moment its feet hit the ground and bolts onto the winding road, footsteps <radical>advance</radical>ing in zigzags, chasing a moth, chasing nothing, laughing the whole way. Running in circles for no reason but joy: that is play.
items.reading_mnemonic: Back at Koichi's konbini, a kid the clerk just calls <reading>You</reading> comes skidding in, sweaty from playing, and yells <reading>ゆう</reading> at every customer like it is a battle cry, delighted with himself, before running back out to play some more.

items.mnemonic_text: Sheep (羊) settling onto the eye's (目) view: to arrive, to wear.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>sheep</radical> arrives dragging a scratchy coat that snagged on its horns on the way over, plants its four stiff crossed legs on the doormat, and refuses to go one step further. The <radical>eye</radical> in the peephole, pupil pinched wide, watches the coat finally settle onto its back — the sheep has arrived, and now it is wearing the thing.
items.reading_mnemonic: At that same door, a courier named <reading>Chaku</reading> stamps the delivery slip and shouts <reading>ちゃく</reading> — arrived — before shoving the parcel at the sheep's hooves and speeding off, coat and all, without waiting for a signature.

items.mnemonic_text: A road (辶) that splits away (韋): to differ.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A disembodied <radical>mouth</radical> plants itself at a fork in the road and bellows directions with total confidence, left, while your own footsteps quietly <radical>advance</radical> right instead, because the mouth's directions never match where the road goes. Two opinions, two paths: that is what it means to differ.
items.reading_mnemonic: On the mountain trail, a hiker named <reading>E</reading> takes the mouth's directions and immediately regrets it, stubbing her toe on a root and yelping <reading>い</reading>, which is exactly the sound of finding out, one more time, that the two of you always end up disagreeing.

items.mnemonic_text: A bird (隹) landing on a tree (木) with the flock: to gather.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Word gets out on some pigeon grapevine, and by dusk every <radical>old bird</radical> in town has shuffled onto the same <radical>tree</radical>, wings too stiff to fly, hopping branch to branch until the whole trunk is buried under molting, dust-covered old birds refusing to leave — the tree has gathered every last one of them.
items.reading_mnemonic: Up in the branches, an arborist swats at the crowd of old birds and yells <reading>Shoo</reading>, <reading>しゅう</reading>, but not one bird moves off the tree — there are too many, and shooing just isn't going to cut it today.

items.mnemonic_text: A knife (刂) cutting a shape (另) apart: to separate.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The little rabbit is still buttering toast with its <radical>sword</radical> when a flexed <radical>power</radical>ful arm grabs the loaf and yanks, and a gaping <radical>mouth</radical> closes over half of it before the blade lands. Loaf ripped one way, sword swinging the other: one thing is now unmistakably two, kept separate.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the riverbank, someone waves off half a delivery, handing it to a woman named <reading>Betsy</reading> and calling out <reading>べつ</reading>: separate boat, separate load. The rabbit's loaf and its missing half drift downstream in different currents.

items.mnemonic_text: A lamp's flame steady atop its stand: the main, central one.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Three cheap flat <radical>king / jewel</radical> crowns wobble, skewered by one iron spike, and just as the pile threatens to slide off, a single <radical>drop</radical> of wax falls from the chandelier and seals the topmost crown in place. That fused, unmistakable stack is the one everyone bows to — the main one, the lord of the room.
items.reading_mnemonic: Back on the throne, the king's valet holds up the lord's one remaining polished <reading>shoe</reading> and announces <reading>しゅ</reading> to the court — the shoe proves who's still the main one in charge, wax-sealed crown and all.
items.description: 主 differs from 王 by exactly one mark: 主 adds a small drop stroke sitting above the top horizontal line, before the three stacked bars begin, while 王 has no dot at all — just the three flat crowns and the single spike through the middle, nothing above the topmost bar.

items.mnemonic_text: A mouth (口) atop legs (儿): the elder brother who speaks first.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Someone stands wide-legged in the doorway, plants both <radical>human legs</radical> shoulder-width apart like they own the place, then throws back a gaping <radical>mouth</radical> and yawns loud enough that you are the one who deals with whatever woke everyone up. Only an older brother yawns like the world owes him a nap.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the school gate, a kid jerks a thumb toward your family and sneers that's <reading>Kay</reading>'s little sibling, <reading>けい</reading> being the older brother everyone already knows by reputation, before you have even said a word.

items.mnemonic_text: A cord wound down a post: the younger, lower-ranked brother.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your little brother sneaks off with your <radical>bow</radical>, and instead of just using it he wraps loose cord round and round the curved wood in messy loops, showing off to nobody. That reckless kid overusing your gear, dragging the string wherever he goes, is exactly what a younger brother looks like.
items.reading_mnemonic: That same reckless kid trips over his own tangled bowstring and yelps <reading>Tay</reading>, <reading>てい</reading>, don't tell mom, already looping a second cord before anyone can drag him back inside for dinner.

items.mnemonic_text: A woman (女) who is already (市-like) senior: the older sister.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At the riverbank, the <radical>woman</radical> catches herself mid-spin, drapes a folded <radical>cloth</radical> over her shoulders like a cape, then rams a <radical>lid</radical> down onto her head as a makeshift hat, and marches off ordering the younger kids about their washing — that swaggering self-appointed supervisor is your older sister.
items.reading_mnemonic: Back at the river, she silences the squabbling kids with one sharp <reading>し</reading> — a hissed <reading>shh</reading> that cuts through the splashing instantly — the unmistakable sound of an older sister taking charge.
items.description: Don't confuse this with 妹, the kanji for younger sister. Here the right side stacks a lid over a hanging fold of cloth, a cap over drapery. In 妹 the right side is a tree with an extra short stroke near the top, giving two branches instead of one. Cap-over-cloth is older; two branches is younger.

items.mnemonic_text: A woman (女) not yet (未) grown: the younger sister.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Up on the mountain trail, the same crossed-limbed <radical>woman</radical> from the dance turns up tangled sideways in a <radical>tree</radical>, arms still flung wide, giggling and refusing to climb down until someone catches her — that reckless, easily rescued climber is your younger sister.
items.reading_mnemonic: Below her, someone shouts that she'll fall, and all she yells back, upside down and gleeful, is a stretched-out <reading>まい</reading> — <reading>my</reading> turn, not yet! — before slipping another branch lower.
items.description: Don't confuse this with 姉, the kanji for older sister. Here the right side is a tree with an extra short stroke near the top, giving two branches instead of one. The right side of 姉 instead stacks a lid over a hanging fold of cloth, a cap over drapery. Two branches is younger; cap-over-cloth is older.

items.mnemonic_text: Standing (立) by a tree (木) watching (見): a parent's love.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At the edge of Sei's school field, someone has climbed a <radical>tree</radical> and wedged themselves upright to <radical>stand</radical> on the highest branch, craning forward to <radical>see</radical> every second of the match without missing a single kick — that worried, straining figure who won't leave until it's over is a parent.
items.reading_mnemonic: When the final whistle blows, they scramble down too fast and bark their <reading>しん</reading> — their <reading>shin</reading> — hard against a branch, then limp off still cheering about the goal.

items.mnemonic_text: A person kneeling beside a seal: the color of one's mood.
items.meaning_mnemonic: That same stubborn <radical>wrap</radical> from the gift-wrapper's parcel turns up at the dye vat, one cloth edge overlapping to hold the steam in. Inside, red, indigo, and yellow threads writhe together, straining against that lopsided wrap until it slips loose. They spill out tangled into one impossible bolt of color.
items.reading_mnemonic: A dye-shop apprentice grabs the vat's exposed wire without thinking and gets a jolt of <reading>shock</reading>, yelping <reading>しょく</reading> as sparks scatter across the wet, rainbow-streaked threads still steaming on the table.

items.mnemonic_text: A mouth (口) not yet (未) full: tasting a bit.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At Koichi's konbini, someone bites into an onigiri and a whole <radical>tree</radical>, roots and all, comes sprouting straight out of their <radical>mouth</radical>, branches waving over the shelf — the stocker doesn't even look up, because that violent, involuntary reaction is exactly what taste does to a person here.
items.reading_mnemonic: He clutches his throat and manages only one strangled syllable, <reading>み</reading> — it comes out sounding just like <reading>me</reading> — before diving for the drink fridge to wash the flavor down.

items.mnemonic_text: A woman (女) beside her child (子): a fondness, to like.
items.meaning_mnemonic: That bundled-up <radical>child</radical>, arms thrown wide, comes barreling down the konbini aisle and collides with the <radical>woman</radical> stocking the shelf, one leg still crossed mid-step from catching her balance. She doesn't scold him — she wraps her flung-wide arms around him and holds on, delighted. That's what liking someone looks like.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi, the konbini king, watches from the till and tries to <reading>coax</reading> the toddler back with a sticker, murmuring <reading>こう</reading>, <reading>こう</reading> — but the kid's already found someone better to hug, so Koichi just restocks the onigiri instead.

items.mnemonic_text: A twisted shape over the heart (心): a bad feeling.
items.meaning_mnemonic: That same fishhook-shaped <radical>heart</radical>, still flinging its three drops of blood from the barb, gets swallowed whole by a stray cat behind the shrine. It doesn't turn the cat mean — it just makes everything the cat does afterward go wrong: knocked-over bins, hissing at nothing, one long streak of trouble. That's what a bad heart does.
items.reading_mnemonic: The cat, still hissing, gets its tail pinned under a fallen bin and yowls in pure <reading>awkward</reading> pain — <reading>あく</reading> — echoing off the shrine steps before it slinks away, guiltier than ever.

items.mnemonic_text: Big (大) with an extra drop of size: thick, fat.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture a person standing with arms flung wide and legs spread in a huge X, filling the whole page. A single <radical>drop</radical> - a ladle of stew, not water - plops right onto his belly and soaks straight in. His stomach swells outward on the spot, arms pushed even wider by his own gut. That one dropped ladle is the difference between big and thick, fat.
items.reading_mnemonic: The cook who ladled that stew is a heavyset chef named <reading>Tai</reading>. He pats his own swollen belly, proud of the extra drop he added, and sighs <reading>たい</reading>, satisfied at how thick he's made himself.
items.description: 太 is 大 (big) with one extra dot. On 太 that dot sits low, tucked between the legs where the stew dripped in - the mark of something thickened. On 犬 (dog) the dot instead sits high, off the right arm, like a tail flicked up and out. Same big-person shape, different spot for the single drop.

items.mnemonic_text: Thread (糸) drawn out fine over a field (田): thin, detailed.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Someone strings a single strand of <radical>thread</radical> straight across your entire <radical>rice field</radical>, tying it paddy to paddy as a property line. Stretched taut over that whole distance, the strand pulls thinner and thinner until it all but vanishes against the green - thin, fine, barely there at all.
items.reading_mnemonic: Farmer <reading>Sai</reading> walks the paddy edge every morning, running a finger along the line to find it. Each time he loses sight of it in the grass he mutters <reading>さい</reading>, annoyed at how thin the thing is.

items.mnemonic_text: A cart (車) that passes lightly (圣): not heavy.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A heavy wooden <radical>vehicle</radical> rolls past hauling a full mound of <radical>earth</radical>. Every lap around the yard, that same <radical>again</radical> hand reaches in and steals one more scoop off the top. The cart rattles back a little higher on its wheels each time, bouncing more and more, until it's rolling along light as nothing.
items.reading_mnemonic: The scooping culprit is a stablehand named <reading>Kei</reading>, who can't stop himself. Each time the cart bounces higher he grins and mutters <reading>けい</reading> under his breath, delighted at how light he's made it.

items.mnemonic_text: A cart's heavy load stacked high: heavy, important.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your whole <radical>village</radical> - every paddy stacked on its slab of packed earth - gets loaded onto a scale. Behind it the <radical>day</radical>'s sun keeps climbing, glaring through its little window without a single cloud. The needle won't budge, because underneath it all sits one slab of <radical>ground</radical>, unmoving. The whole village is simply heavy.
items.reading_mnemonic: The ox pulling the scale, a stubborn animal named <reading>Joo</reading>, plants its hooves and refuses to shift. Villagers push and it just groans <reading>じゅう</reading>, sinking deeper into the ground instead.
items.description: 重 stacks a sun-window box (日) over the village grid (里) on top of a ground line - three pieces, tall and busy. 車 is only the simple cart shape: one box crossed top and bottom by a single line, with two wheel bars sticking out the sides - lean and symmetric where 重 is layered and heavy-looking.

items.mnemonic_text: Two bent bows losing their tension: weak.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At the top of the mountain trail, an archer draws her <radical>bow</radical>, but overnight <radical>ice</radical> has crept along the wood, gluing the string stiff against the frame. She hauls back with everything she has and the string only creaks, then sags loose the instant she lets go — the arrow drops dead at her own boots. Weak.
items.reading_mnemonic: Halfway down that same icy trail, a hiker named <reading>Jock</reading> collapses against a boulder, legs shaking, and moans <reading>じゃく</reading>, じゃく, over and over, while the frozen bow slides out of his numb fingers into the snow.

items.mnemonic_text: A bow (弓) reinforced with a hard shell (虽): strong.
items.meaning_mnemonic: In the gym locker room, a <radical>cocoon</radical> sealing itself shut suddenly rips open — not a silkworm this time but a rhinoceros beetle forcing its way out, <radical>insect</radical>-strong. It snatches a <radical>bow</radical> leaning against the lockers and bends it double for a dare, the wood groaning under six stubborn legs. Strong.
items.reading_mnemonic: Back in the locker room, a boy named <reading>Kyo</reading> stares at the bent bow and mutters <reading>きょう</reading>, きょう, over and over, unable to believe a beetle just out-arm-wrestled the entire soccer team.

items.mnemonic_text: The sun (日) hidden behind sound (音) of night: dark.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At Grandma Kane's shrine, the little <radical>sun</radical> behind its two-bar window is just climbing to start the day when the biggest cat on the steps rears up on its hind legs to <radical>stand</radical> chest-first in the doorway, paws braced wide like it owns the place. Its shadow swallows the whole window in one go, and the mossy steps drop into dark.
items.reading_mnemonic: Grandma Kane fumbles for the huge bell in the sudden dark and rings it anyway, and from behind the cat a startled visitor named <reading>Anne</reading> gasps <reading>あん</reading>, あん, can't see a thing, groping past fur to find the steps.

items.mnemonic_text: The sun (日) beside the moon (月): both lighting up, bright.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At Grandma Kane's shrine at dawn, two windows glow in the mossy wall. Through the one-barred pane climbs the blazing <radical>sun</radical>, starting the day. Through the two-barred pane beside it hangs the pale <radical>moon</radical>, refusing to set. Sun and moon blazing through both windows at once floods the courtyard so bright the cats squint — this is bright.
items.reading_mnemonic: Outside the gate stands a tourist named May, camera raised at the blinding courtyard. She keeps muttering <reading>めい</reading>, <reading>May</reading>, hunting for the word for bright and finding only her own name, so she just points at the glare instead.

items.mnemonic_text: A shelter (广) opening onto open ground: wide, spacious.
items.meaning_mnemonic: That cliffside <radical>shelter</radical> turns out to be absurdly wide — its diagonal roof floats over so much open air that a whole field fits underneath with room to spare. A silkworm tries to seal itself into a <radical>cocoon</radical> in one corner, spinning the closing loop again and again, but the space is too wide for it to ever meet the other edge. Wide.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi surveys his newly renovated konbini — the fluorescent aisles now stretch so wide he needs a golf cart to reach the onigiri shelf. He beams at the beeping till and announces, <reading>こう</reading>, this is what real square footage feels like, pure <reading>Koh</reading>-style efficiency at last.

items.mnemonic_text: Water (氵) breaking through a levee (夬): a decisive break.
items.meaning_mnemonic: On the mountain trail, a hiker stalls at a signpost where the path forks, a borrowed marker brush still dripping in her hand. She flicks the wet bristles — three <radical>water</radical> droplets fly off in a row and splash across the left arrow, blotting the right one out completely. Case closed: she follows whichever arrow is still legible. Decided.
items.reading_mnemonic: Perched on the signpost, a marmot named Ketch watches the paint drip and chitters <reading>けつ</reading>, <reading>Ketch</reading>, approving her choice before scrambling down the now-legible path ahead of her.

items.mnemonic_text: An old man's (耂) bent posture, deep in thought.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At the crosswalk, that stooped, unhurried <radical>old</radical> man stops dead in the middle, one hand cupped like the lopsided <radical>wrap</radical> that never quite fits the watermelon — except now it's cupped around his own chin. Traffic idles as he turns something over, wrapping his cane-slow mind around a problem before taking another step. That's thinking.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi, the konbini king, spots the old man frozen mid-crosswalk and can't restock the onigiri shelf until he moves. A crow on the awning tips its head and <reading>caws</reading> — <reading>こう</reading> — the exact sound of someone thinking too hard to hurry.

items.mnemonic_text: Words (言) matched all around (周): to check, investigate.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At Koichi's konbini, the till keeps beeping over a missing onigiri. The manager lines up three suspects and cups his ear at each one in turn. Every time a mouth opens, another stack of horizontal <radical>speech</radical> bubbles rises off it, alibi after alibi piling higher than the shelf, until one stack cracks and the truth spills out. Investigate.
items.reading_mnemonic: Behind the register stands a beat cop named Chow, notebook open, tallying every stacked bubble. He grunts <reading>ちょう</reading>, <reading>Chow</reading>, each time a suspect's story shifts, until his tally points straight at the onigiri thief hiding behind the till.

items.mnemonic_text: Feathers (羽) over white (白): a bird practicing to fly, to learn.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At the riverbank, a duckling flings itself off a rock trying to fly. Each failed launch yanks loose a matching pair of stiff <radical>feather</radical> plumes drifting onto the water. It keeps aiming for one bright bead of milk on a lilypad, glinting <radical>white</radical> in the sun. Attempt after attempt, feathers scattering, glint still out of reach — that relentless repeating is learn and practice.
items.reading_mnemonic: A birdwatcher named Shoe sits on the bank with a clipboard, tally marks climbing with every failed launch. She murmurs <reading>しゅう</reading>, <reading>Shoe</reading> under her breath at each attempt, certain the duckling will get airborne if it just keeps practicing.

items.mnemonic_text: Learning (⺍) opening one's view (見): to remember, realize.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At Grandma Kane's shrine, the eyeball-on-legs that wanders to <radical>see</radical> everything creeps toward the enormous bell. Someone throws the porch cat's blanket over it — the same snug <radical>cover</radical> that never lets an edge poke out — and it freezes in the dark. In that last blind second the bell's shape burns in so hard it never needs to look again. That is remembering.
items.reading_mnemonic: Under the cloth, the shrine cat in her <reading>khaki</reading> poncho hears the eyeball scrabbling and mutters <reading>かく</reading> at every scratch against the fabric, resigned to washing claw marks out of it again by evening.

items.mnemonic_text: A dying (亡) heart (心) losing its memory: to forget.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At Sei's school, the wounded, thumping <radical>heart</radical> — hook dragging low, three drops flung off the barb — snags on a locker door and stops, mid-beat, whatever it was carrying draining out through the hook like the blood already has. By the time it works itself loose and wobbles on, it cannot recall what it snagged on. That blank, drained heart is forgetting.
items.reading_mnemonic: Down the empty hallway, a ghost named <reading>Bo</reading> drifts past the snagged heart and moans <reading>ぼう</reading>, low and hollow — the exact sound of something that used to matter fading out of a heart's grip entirely.

items.mnemonic_text: A wagon (軍) moving down a road (辶): to carry, one's fortune.
items.meaning_mnemonic: On the mountain trail, someone straps a tarp <radical>cover</radical> over the little <radical>vehicle</radical> — axle, two wheels — so nothing spills, then plants footstep after footstep to <radical>advance</radical> it up the steep climb toward the vending machine at the top. Whatever survives the grind, tarp still snug, wheels still spinning, has been carried — and just arriving on a slope like that counts as pure luck.
items.reading_mnemonic: Halfway up, the hiker hauling the cart — everyone just calls her <reading>Oona</reading> — grunts <reading>うん</reading> with every step, the same sound as her own name, until the vending machine at the top rewards her stubbornness with a drink that isn't even the one she wanted.

items.mnemonic_text: A road (辶) release (关) sending something off: to send.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At the riverbank, a delivery boy plants footstep after footstep onto the muddy road, using it to <radical>advance</radical> right up to the water's edge. He doesn't stop there — he draws his arm back and lets the parcel sail clean across, already turning to walk the same road back. Getting something moving forward until it leaves your hands entirely: that is sending.
items.reading_mnemonic: The boy's only witness is Sow, a pig who lives by the crossing, and every time he lobs a parcel over the water she gives the same unimpressed grunt, <reading>そう</reading> — which sounds exactly like someone muttering <reading>so</reading> to themselves right before they let something go.

items.mnemonic_text: Two axes (斤斤) weighing shells (貝) of value: quality, substance.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The woodsman's <radical>axe</radical> is still buried hilt-deep in the chopping block — that argument's over. A peddler crouches beside it and pries the <radical>money</radical> shell open with both thumbs until coins spill into his palm, turning each one to the light, questioning it, weighing it, before he decides it has the quality worth the trade.
items.reading_mnemonic: The peddler pockets one more coin, but stump sawdust dusts his palm and it starts to itch. Sheesh, itchy, he hisses, shaking his hand out and blowing grit off the last coin, muttering <reading>しつ</reading>, <reading>しつ</reading> — the sound comes out exactly like his <reading>itchy</reading> complaint.

items.mnemonic_text: Bamboo (竹) matching (合) the right response: an answer.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Two stalks of <radical>bamboo</radical> in Sei's schoolyard lean together, leaves flicking like a drumroll. Right between their roots the level <radical>ground</radical> splits along one flat crack, and a wide square <radical>mouth</radical> yawns up out of the gap — not to ask anything, just to blurt out the answer before you've finished asking.
items.reading_mnemonic: Sei stubs her toe on the bamboo root right where the ground cracked open, and yelps instead of answering the teacher's question. Everyone laughs, but the barked <reading>とう</reading> still counts — a stubbed <reading>toe</reading> makes exactly that sound, and gets treated as her answer anyway.

items.mnemonic_text: A flag (方 side) rallying an arrow's (矢) clan together: family.
items.meaning_mnemonic: That same stray <radical>arrow</radical>, still quivering in the vendor's pumpkin, turns out to be signed — feathers dyed the same color every year. Uncles, cousins, and a very unbothered grandmother converge on the fence, each recognizing the fletching as theirs, until a whole clan is crowded around one ruined pumpkin arguing whose family shot it.
items.reading_mnemonic: Grandma stomps up in mismatched <reading>socks</reading>, glaring at the ruined pumpkin, and mutters <reading>ぞく</reading> under her breath before anyone else speaks — the whole family already knows exactly which cousin's arrow this is, just from the socks.

items.mnemonic_text: Rice (米) measured with a dipper (斗): materials, a fee.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At Koichi's konbini, the baker plunges the trusted <radical>dipper</radical> into a sack of <radical>rice</radical>, its grains scattering like a tiny explosion as it comes up loaded and level. He tips it into a paper bag, marks a tally on the register, and charges by the scoop — the material measured out becomes exactly the fee you pay.
items.reading_mnemonic: A customer named <reading>Leo</reading> counts each dipper-load of rice as it clinks into his bag, muttering <reading>りょう</reading>, <reading>りょう</reading> under his breath to keep track of how many scoops he owes, until his tally and the register's total match up, scoop for scoop.

items.mnemonic_text: A jewel (王) cut along its natural grain (里): reason, logic.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>king / jewel</radical> hauls his spiked, jewel-crusted crown into the <radical>village</radical> and rams the spike into the packed earth between the paddies. From there he measures every paddy edge against the spike, rejecting any row that bends even slightly, until the whole village runs on nothing but his cold, straight-line reason.
items.reading_mnemonic: A surveyor named <reading>Reeko</reading> stands where the king planted his spike, snapping her measuring cord taut across the paddies with a sharp <reading>り</reading> every time a farmer's row drifts off the straight line.

items.mnemonic_text: A heart (心) pierced by a single resolved stroke: certainly necessary.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>heart</radical> is still hooked low and flinging its three drops of blood when a cleaver comes down and pins it flat to the altar with one diagonal slash through the middle. Nobody moves it again — a heart nailed down like that isn't optional anymore, it's simply necessary.
items.reading_mnemonic: The shrine boy who nailed it down mutters a chant over the pinned heart, tapping the blade's handle twice for luck, and it comes out as a flat little <reading>ひつ</reading> — like he's clearing his throat, <reading>hit-soo</reading>, before he can walk away.
items.description: 必 is 心 (heart) with one extra diagonal stroke slashing down across the hook from upper left to lower right. Without that slash, the three loose drops sit under a bare fishhook — that plain shape is 心 on its own. With it, the stroke pins straight through the hook, and that pinned, slashed heart is 必.

items.mnemonic_text: A woman (女) under a covering (覀): the essential point, needed.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The talent show can't start without her: the <radical>woman</radical> frozen mid-dance, one leg swung wide and arms flung across her body, is the only act the whole gym is waiting on. Every other performer gets cut from the lineup before her, because without that one dancer nothing here is important enough to keep.
items.reading_mnemonic: Backstage, the stage manager keeps checking his clipboard and groaning <reading>よう</reading>, the same sound he'd make chasing a lost <reading>yo-yo</reading> under the bleachers, because the dancer still hasn't shown up and the whole show needs her.

items.mnemonic_text: Thread (糸) running straight through the loom (圣): to pass through time.
items.meaning_mnemonic: In the temple's back room, the same <radical>right hand</radical> that keeps sneaking into the cookie jar now reaches out <radical>again</radical> and again, feeding a spool of <radical>thread</radical> through a loom staked into the <radical>earth</radical> like a signpost. Row after row, the thread passes through the frame while the monk drones the same sutra over and over, never stopping.
items.reading_mnemonic: The apprentice threading the loom is named <reading>Kay</reading>, and every time the shuttle passes through she exhales a low <reading>けい</reading>, matching the monk's chant beat for beat until the thread and the sutra finish the row together.

items.mnemonic_text: Thread (糸) sold (売) onward without a break: to continue.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Grandma Kane's shrine cat sleeps under its usual <radical>cover</radical>, tucked snug past its ears, but a stray <radical>thread</radical> from the blanket keeps unspooling down the mossy steps. It runs past a pair of <radical>human legs</radical> marching in place, refusing to stop, straight to the <radical>samurai</radical> duck on sentry duty, who salutes and lets the thread run on under his feet rather than break the line. Nothing here ends — it all just continues.
items.reading_mnemonic: At those same shrine steps, a tourist named <reading>Zach</reading> tries to leave but his legs won't quit marching in place, round and round, and every stomp echoes <reading>ぞく</reading> off the mossy stone, on and on, refusing to stop.

items.mnemonic_text: Two people standing side by side: to compare.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Outside Koichi's konbini, two identical clerks stand shoulder to shoulder against the doorframe, backs flat, chins level, each daring the other to be an inch taller. Neither moves, neither blinks — they just stand there side by side under the fluorescent light, forever being compared.
items.reading_mnemonic: One clerk finally cracks and jabs a thumb at himself, shouting <reading>ひ</reading> — insisting <reading>He</reading>'s obviously the taller one — while the other clerk just narrows his eyes and keeps standing there under the konbini lights, refusing to concede an inch.
items.description: 比 almost never stands alone as a word. In everyday use it shows up bound into other kanji or attached as 比べる, and mostly in contexts about ratios and percentages rather than as a freestanding term by itself.

items.mnemonic_text: Feet advancing (辶) among matched (巽) options: to choose.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The mountain trail is the same winding <radical>road</radical> you've been climbing, footsteps advancing step by step toward the summit — except today it forks three ways around the vending machine. You plant one foot on a single fork and commit, ignoring the other two. Deciding which path to advance down is what it means to choose.
items.reading_mnemonic: At that same fork, a hiker named <reading>Sen</reading> freezes completely, muttering <reading>せん</reading> over and over while staring at the vending machine, unable to advance a single step until he finally commits to a path.

items.mnemonic_text: Bones (歹) left over after the cut (戔): what remains.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At the shrine gate, the <radical>halberd</radical> that toppled when a guard's scarf snagged its blade now lies clattered in the dirt, its shaft snapped clean at the joint — a fresh crack of <radical>death / bad luck</radical> running through the wood. Nobody hauls it away; it just stays where it fell, broken but present. Whatever's left after the disaster is what remains.
items.reading_mnemonic: Every morning the shrine's groundskeeper cat, a stubborn old tom named <reading>Zan</reading>, sniffs at the broken halberd and grumbles <reading>ざん</reading>, deciding again it isn't his job to move it — so there it stays.

items.mnemonic_text: Earth (土) piled ever higher (曽): to increase.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The sun climbs behind that windowed bar marking a new <radical>day</radical>, and the farmer eyes his flooded <radical>rice field</radical> creeping past the wooden signpost planted in the <radical>earth</radical> — the plots multiplying past the marker, claiming more ground than yesterday. By sundown there is simply more of everything, mud and water both. That's increase.
items.reading_mnemonic: Back at that same signpost, a farmer named Zo watches the water creep higher up the wood and grunts <reading>ぞう</reading> each time — flat and low, like saying '<reading>zo</reading>' with a shrug. By dusk he's grunted it so many times the whole field has crept higher than the post itself.

items.mnemonic_text: Water (氵) cut down (咸) to less: to decrease.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The guard's <radical>halberd</radical> clatters down as a scarf yanks it off the gate, knocking over a cup — <radical>water</radical> flicks out drop by drop, like droplets off a wet brush, spattering into a waiting <radical>mouth</radical> below that gulps each one down. By the last drop the cup stands empty. That's decrease.
items.reading_mnemonic: Watching his cup drain past his open mouth, the guard groans <reading>げん</reading> between gulps — flat, like saying '<reading>gen</reading>' each time the water level drops. One groan per gulp, and there's less in the cup with every single one.

items.mnemonic_text: Threads (糸-like) twisted into something strange: to change.
items.meaning_mnemonic: That duckling still towed by its own bootlace, <radical>trailing foot</radical> skidding along the floor, finally snags the knob of a <radical>lid</radical> resting on a pot ahead. Everything flips — duckling and lid spin together, and when they land the lid is clamped backwards over its head like a crown. Nothing about the scene matches how it started. That's change.
items.reading_mnemonic: Watching this spin from the doorway, a chicken named <reading>Hen</reading> squawks <reading>へん</reading> in pure disbelief, the same flat sound as her own name, as the duckling waddles off wearing the pot lid like a crown.
items.description: This kanji doubles as a common na-adjective meaning strange or odd, not just change — context decides which sense is meant, and native speakers reach for that second sense constantly.

items.mnemonic_text: A dog (犬) squeezing back under a door (戸): to return.
items.meaning_mnemonic: That raccoon that rammed shoulder-first through the <radical>door</radical>, scraping its tail on the sill as it barreled into the kitchen, doesn't stop there. It circles the block, and twenty minutes later barges back through that same battered door, right where it started, tail scraping the sill all over again. That's return.
items.reading_mnemonic: Next door, a neighbor named Ray sighs <reading>れい</reading> every time he hears the door bang, flat and resigned, like counting the raccoon's laps with a low '<reading>ray</reading>'. Sure enough, a beat later, it barrels back through, right on cue.
items.description: This kanji's on'yomi is genuinely rare in modern Japanese. Outside a handful of fixed compounds, it overwhelmingly appears with its kun'yomi reading instead, so lean on that reading first in real text you encounter.

items.mnemonic_text: A body (尸) stretching (由) out to reach: to deliver, arrive.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Guests keep stepping around the sprawled <radical>corpse / body</radical>, and nobody expects him to move for the doorbell. So when a package arrives, the courier just drags the whole box across the tatami until it bumps his outstretched leg — the only way anything ever reaches him tonight. It has been delivered.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the same party, a courier named <reading>Kai</reading> keeps sighing <reading>かい</reading> as he hauls yet another box across the tatami to the sprawled body's leg, resigned to the fact that delivery here always means dragging, never handing.
